summary: This diff adds a last-owner/admin demotion guard to PATCH /api/org-members/[id] (the sole endpoint in the codebase that can mutate memberships.role, confirmed by a real grep sweep of every DELETE/mutation handler), plus a small batch of previously-ungated PM_OR_ABOVE/FIELD role checks on change-orders, project-budgets, purchase-orders, schedule/baselines, site-diary, and punch-list routes carried over from the PR #53 audit round. The core guard logic is correct: it fetches the target membership's current role, and only blocks the transition when the target is currently owner/admin, the new role is not owner/admin, and no other owner/admin remains in the org (owner<->admin reassignment and reassignment of already-non-admin members are never blocked). Verified independently rather than trusting PROGRESS.md: npx tsc --noEmit is clean and npx eslint on the changed files reports zero errors/warnings (bun was unavailable in this review sandbox so the bun test suite itself could not be re-run here, but the test files type-check and the assertions read correctly against the route's actual logic). The drizzle/0012 migration is a straightforward additive check-constraint change (adds pm/site_engineer/client_viewer to the existing owner/admin/member set) consistent with this repo's migration convention, and schema.ts uses a plain text column with no enum to keep in sync. No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard workflow-scope rule does not apply. One non-blocking design note for the human reviewer below (TOCTOU race between the read-count-update steps), and note per PROGRESS.md that this branch is intended to land on top of PR #53 rather than standalone against main, requiring rebase/ordering reconciliation.
issues: Minor TOCTOU race: the last-owner/admin count check and the subsequent update are not run in a single transaction/atomic constraint, so two concurrent PATCH requests each demoting a different owner/admin at the exact last-two-remaining point could both read a stale 'count=1 other admin' and both succeed, leaving zero owners/admins. Low real-world likelihood (rare admin action, small orgs) but worth a follow-up (e.g. a DB-level trigger/constraint or serializable transaction) if this needs to be airtight rather than best-effort.
This branch is built on top of unmerged PR #53's branch (locally merged in, not rebased) per PROGRESS.md -- a human needs to reconcile merge order before this can land on main standalone.
